name: Baicapil
lead: Baicapil is a branded cosmetic hair-care active marketed for scalp hair-loss serums. Its name suggests a baicalin-based ingredient, and baicalin is a flavone glycoside found in Scutellaria (skullcap) species.[2]

A 2025 trichology review lists Baicapil among the topical actives it examines, and describes such ingredients as heavily promoted on social media.[1] The sources reviewed contain no detail on Baicapil's composition, manufacturer or controlled trial results, so this article is brief.

paras: No studies found. A 2025 review names Baicapil among topical hair actives but the review abstract does not report a trial specific to it.[1]

Baicalin is the glucuronide of baicalein, occurs in Scutellaria baicalensis and related species, and is reported in laboratory and animal work to act as a modulator of GABA-A receptors and to inhibit prolyl endopeptidase.[2] The Wikipedia article on baicalin does not mention hair or hair growth.[2]

card.note: Little published evidence specific to the product.

quick.overview:
Baicapil is a branded ingredient sold in hair-loss serums, linked to baicalin, a plant flavonoid from skullcap.

It is named in a 2025 review of cosmeceutical hair actives; no dedicated human trial was found.
quick.mechanism: Baicalin has been studied for other effects in laboratory work; no mechanism for hair growth is established in the sources reviewed.
quick.risks: No safety data specific to the product were found. It is sold as a cosmetic ingredient.
